response.sql: WITH invoiced_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, c.gender FROM Invoices AS i JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id), gender_counts AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS invoiced_order_count FROM invoiced_orders GROUP BY gender), gender_shares AS (SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, 1.0 * invoiced_order_count / SUM(invoiced_order_count) OVER () AS share FROM gender_counts), compared AS (SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM gender_shares) SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, share, share - average_share AS above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share

assumptions.assumption: An order with multiple invoices counts once. NULL gender, if present, forms its own group.

alternatives.interpretation: Count invoice records instead, so an order with multiple invoices contributes multiple times.
